* Explorer API src/contracts.ts userSchema requires contactId > 0; src/tenant.service.ts putUser directly mutates authority users. PlatformGuard in src/auth.ts restricts published tenant routes to allowlisted platform administrators. No published main-manager role/invitation permission model.

Use “Manager einladen” within a clearly named club, Email as default and “Clerk-Benutzer-ID” as advanced mode. Role is fixed “Vereinsmanager”; never expose arbitrary permission strings. Show club + recipient + expiry before sending. Known-ID resolution is server-side, exact lookup only, minimally masked confirmation; no searchable user directory. Resend rotates the link and tells the manager the previous link expires. Revoke pending access with clear confirmation. Landing flow: minimal club invitation -> Register/Sign in through Clerk -> authenticated confirmation showing club and role -> “Einladung annehmen” -> authorized setup destination. No GET grants access; email scanners cannot consume links. Wrong-account state offers account switch/verify intended email; expired/revoked/tampered state offers a request-new-invitation explanation without exposing recipient data. Same recipient retry returns the prior result; other identities cannot use an already accepted link. Preserve context across auth and refresh using an opaque server-bound flow and fixed allowlisted return paths; never arbitrary redirects. Mobile one-column layout, labelled controls, focus on errors, live loading status, keyboard actions. Resume onboarding per tenant; completed tenants go to club management.

Bexio UX recommendation for decision: acceptance records verified issuer+subject with “Vereinssetup ausstehend”; later connect Bexio -> search/select an existing tenant contact -> explicitly create only when none is suitable -> confirm linkage. Do not auto-match/create solely by email. Validate contact in that exact tenant/provider account, record linkage audit, and handle concurrent creation/linking. This recommendation does NOT resolve question 10031 without Lolo/Chris approval.

### Contract / Solution Architecture Building Block outline for Chris

Preferred candidate: control-plane invitation + restricted onboarding membership, separate from operational runtime authority. Reuse existing provisioning tenant ID, avoid a second draft-tenant system unless APP-26 needs pre-tenant club applications. Alternative: accept into an onboarding-principal record and publish runtime membership only after contact mapping. Reject placeholder contactId and auto-active direct grants. Proposed contract families (route names provisional): tenant-scoped create/list/resend/revoke under separately authorized platform/club APIs; minimal opaque-link preview; authenticated POST acceptance accessible before operational tenant membership; GET/PATCH onboarding state for that exact accepted tenant. Acceptance returns membershipId, tenantId, onboarding state and a server-selected next destination, not unrestricted permissions. Known-ID requests bind expected tenant Clerk issuer + subject; email requests bind intended verified email and issuer. Backend fixes permitted role; client cannot grant permissions.

Invitation record: id, environment, tenantId, expectedIssuer, recipient discriminated email/subject, role, inviter issuer+subject, tokenHash/version, expiresAt, pending/accepted/revoked state, accepted issuer+subject/time, revision; separate delivery attempts/outbox and onboarding state. Token hashing, no-store/referrer policy, URL/log redaction, bounded preview metadata, per-inviter/tenant/IP rate limits and minimal audit identifiers. No token/email payloads in routine logs.

Acceptance must transactionally recheck invitation status/version/expiry/recipient and tenant lifecycle, enforce unique tenant+issuer+subject membership, consume once, append audit and return the same outcome for same-recipient retries. Concurrent acceptance/revoke/resend must serialize through conditional revision updates/transaction. Membership removal must not be undone by replay. Delivery uses durable intent/retry independent of acceptance; resend supersedes old token. Chris must define encrypted delivery-payload handling, retry limits and uncertain provider outcomes.

1. Is initial bootstrap invitation platform-operator-only, with existing main managers allowed to invite additional managers? How is “main” owner represented and delegated?
2. Approve or reject deferring Bexio mapping with a strictly setup-only accepted identity; which setup actions must be allowed before Bexio connection? Choose restricted membership versus separate onboarding principal.

Invitation: pending -> accepted OR revoked; expiry is evaluated server-side. Delivery queued/accepted-by-provider/failed is separate.  
Manager: no membership -> accepted/setup-only -> ready-for-review -> operational. Revoked/disabled access overrides every state. “Owner” identifies the first accepted bootstrap manager; Chris must prevent simultaneous first-owner claims.

### Identity and API contract

Address normalization must be one consistent documented function. Wrong issuer/account gives generic failure.

Same-origin mutation protection and restricted CORS; no-store and no-referrer on link flow, scrub token URL early, redact ingress/app/analytics logs.

### Persistence, concurrency and delivery

Invitation: random 256-bit token, hash-only verifier, seven-day expiry enforced on every acceptance, tokenVersion, recipient discriminant, expectedIssuer, fixed role, inviter, status/revision, accepted identity/time. OnboardingPrincipal unique (environment,tenant,issuer,subject); owner reservation unique (environment,tenant). Tenant onboarding has versioned step evidence/readiness hash, not only client flags.  
Mongo transaction/conditional revision serializes accept/resend/revoke and owner claim. Accepted same-identity retry returns original result without resurrecting revoked membership; another identity denied. Resend invalidates old token atomically. Runtime grant publication and onboarding completion commit with authority revision/audit in same control transaction; unique membership prevents duplicate grants. Unknown commit result is resolved by idempotency lookup, not repeated grant creation. Outbox send is outside transaction, with encrypted short-lived link payload and bounded retry; plaintext token never in audit. SMTP timeout is unknown delivery, not success; retry same message/link; explicit resend creates new version. Revoke invalidates pending link; accepted access revocation is a separate operation revoking setup principal AND runtime grant. Tenant suspension/disable overrides setup and operational access; provisioning allows setup only.

ContactId is scoped to tenant AND verified Bexio account/connection revision. Reconnect to a different account invalidates mapping/readiness; never preserve numeric-ID trust across accounts. Setup lookup is read-only, bounded and minimal. No auto-link/create from email. The selected contact can convey Bexio-derived privileges, so later invitees must not freely choose a privileged identity: recommend main manager selects/confirms mapping, recipient acknowledges. Bootstrap owner may select own contact after proving connection to the club account, with explicit confirmation/audit; no hidden contact role mutation. Recommend existing-contact selection only for first release; missing contact created in Bexio by authorized person, then retry.

APP-27 owns invitation/acceptance/setup admission, not implicit delivery of APP-26 wizard. APP-26 owns step schema, persistence and completion manifest. Other operational account/category/article/service prerequisites are deployment/workflow-specific. A versioned server readiness manifest must enumerate them and keep unsupported workflows disabled. Separate machine bootstrap from human administrator authorization to avoid a circular login dependency. Current env-based admin UI cannot be treated as already compliant with this story. This is design evidence, not authorization to modify live identity/credentials.

Chris-role gate: APPROVED cloud architecture direction and implementation of this story's security controls. User's own key-vault-api/key-vault-app remain the secret authority. Workload identity authenticates cloud callers; no operator-managed application secrets/static vault tokens in Vercel environment settings. Includes key-vault-app's own Clerk bootstrap without circular human-login dependency. Reviewed SABB docs/APP-36-SABB-approved.md in APP-36 isolated delivery branch/chat. Attribution: Chris-role review under authenticated Lolo, not Chris-account authentication.

Current local loopback service must not simply be exposed publicly. No live infrastructure/credentials/migration/deploy/merge performed or authorized by this gate. Story stays To Do for coordinator planning; APP-36 local implementation may proceed independently under its approved SABB.

## Chris — cloud hardening solution, initial review

User requested APP-47 work alongside APP-36. **Direction approved; cloud deployment remains BLOCKED.** APP-36 stays local-only with its existing startup/restart policy. This review does not change that contract.

**Verified gaps:** key-vault-api HEAD `65d40b0` validates/binds loopback HTTP, authorizes static scoped tokens, loads a plaintext bootstrap master key and Mongo URI from the host environment. It already uses AES-GCM with namespace/revision AAD, majority writes and revision CAS; these are worth retaining, but do not detect restoration of an older valid database. key-vault-app still accepts a pasted browser grant and reads Clerk secrets from env. No cloud authentication or admin model should be inferred from those local protections.

### Recommended building blocks

* **Hosting candidate:** persistent container service with at least one warm instance, controlled HTTPS ingress and private Mongo connectivity. Azure Container Apps with managed identity is a practical candidate, not a selected/purchased provider. Keep our API/database as the application-secret authority. An infrastructure KMS may protect only the vault root: host identity unwraps an encrypted master-key envelope during bootstrap; Mongo bootstrap credentials require separately protected infrastructure custody. Never fetch these roots from the locked vault. Software master/application keys remain readable in vault process memory; this does not make them HSM-nonexportable. [Managed identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/managed-identity), [root wrapping operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/about-keys-details).
* **Workload gateway inside vault:** use platform OIDC directly, avoiding a new token issuer. Fixed issuer/JWKS and vault-specific audience; strict algorithm/lifetime checks, exact owner_id/project_id/environment grants, deny preview/development for production. Headers select a requested namespace, never confer authority. Map each reviewed workload to finite read-only process/shared/tenant capabilities; no list/write/admin unless separately granted. Static tokens remain local-mode only. Vercel supplies an official runtime token API and immutable identity claims. [API](https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/api), [claims](https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/reference).
* **Human admin BFF:** machine identity may fetch ONLY its own Clerk/bootstrap namespace before login. After login, enforce explicit operator RBAC, step-up for destructive/reveal actions, same-origin/CSRF protections and per-operation namespace checks. Do not exchange every signed-in user for the BFF's broad authority. Remove pasted static tokens in cloud mode. No secrets in browser builds; prove Node/proxy bootstrap works before choosing Vercel for this UI, otherwise host the UI with a controlled server bootstrap.
* **Storage/operations:** retain authenticated envelopes and atomic versioned named-set reads from APP-36. Add cloud root-envelope versioning, private TLS DB accounts, durable external redacted audit, encrypted backups and restore exercises, dependency patching and emergency deny/recycle procedures. Separate runtime, provisioning, rotation and recovery identities. AAD/CAS alone cannot prevent valid-snapshot rollback; retain an external generation/recovery checkpoint.

### Proposed cloud policies and delivery slices

1. Implement disabled-by-default cloud configuration, OIDC verification/authorization and transport adapters with forged/wrong issuer/audience/project/environment/namespace/expiry/unknown-key tests. Fixed JWKS destinations, bounded refresh/cache; deny unverifiable requests. Never weaken local Host/Origin guards globally.
2. Add TLS/proxy trust boundaries, no direct-origin bypass, request/deadline/concurrency/crypto limits, readiness and redacted audit. Review admin UX with Freddie. Secrets stay server-only; no wildcard CORS or public caches.
3. Cloud consumers use a proposed **15-minute maximum secret-generation lease**, renewed by authenticated revalidation; on expiry/outage stop new protected work. Rotation changes require coherent generation replacement/recycle, not mixed versions. Emergency revocation blocks new reads immediately at the vault but cannot recall exported secrets; provider revocation and forced recycling are required. This policy needs owner approval and is deliberately separate from APP-36 unlimited post-start local memory use. Test OIDC renewal on warm instances, cold starts, Clerk bootstrap and no-secret builds. Vercel function tokens are documented as two hours; never assume a process-start token stays valid indefinitely.
4. Prove atomic reads under concurrent rotation, old-ciphertext recovery, dependency outages and isolated backup restore; Trip validates exact heads, then Lolo approves activation. No live migration/key generation/provisioning/deployment in this investigation.

**Decisions needed for deployment:** hosting region/operator and root custody (including permission to use infrastructure KMS solely for root wrapping), actual owner/project/namespace matrix, and finite lease/recovery targets. Initial proposed targets: 5s startup-read deadline with bounded jittered retries; no readiness until complete snapshot; RPO 24h/RTO 4h subject to restore proof. Architecture work can continue while these are selected. No Jarvis deployment handoff or release approval yet. Source/docs analysis only; no services or credentials changed.

# APP-49 — Application-managed vault configuration

Status: proposed design for user approval and Chris architecture/security review.  
Prepared by Codex in delivery chat `01a19bed-7679-7bc3-9e6a-130bf59b6de1`.  
This document includes source analysis and the Freddie-stage UX proposal; it does  
not claim an independent Freddie review or Chris approval. No implementation is  
authorized by this document. APP-9 is excluded.

## Agreed product behavior

User decisions in APP-49 comments 10139, 10143 and 10144:

* Create Applications in the UI and link existing secrets/keys through managed  
  application membership and ENV-name metadata. Inspect every linked resource  
  and its tags from its Application page.
* Bootstrap requires application name and grants, using existing/default vault  
  connection configuration. No command-line plan creation or manual revisions.
* Sharing secrets across applications must work. Each logical secret has one  
  canonical ENV variable name, identical in every consuming application.
* Latest is the normal default; optional exact-version pinning remains advanced.
* Both secret and encryption-key changes propagate automatically. The user  
  accepted up to five seconds for normal adoption without a restart.
* A failed refresh retains the last working configuration and shows a warning.

The five-second target versus long-running cryptographic migrations is an open  
product clarification described below, not a silently approved exception.

## Source baseline and boundaries

Vault API development at `e585422`; both vault primaries matched fetched  
origin/development during analysis. The app's existing `next-env.d.ts` edit was  
left untouched. There were no open PRs in either vault repository.

* `docs/STARTUP-MANIFESTS.md`, `runtime-client/index.cjs`: application startup  
  discovery already removes consumer `LOCAL_KEYVAULT_BINDINGS_JSON`. Manifests,  
  values and dependent clients remain cached until restart.
* `src/runtime-manifest-plan.ts`: the administrator still supplies a plan and  
  positive revisions. Multiple versions without a pin produce AmbiguousVersion.  
  Current secret lookup derives names from purpose rather than arbitrary IDs.
* `src/runtime-manifests.ts`, `src/runtime-snapshot.ts`: immutable manifest history,  
  digest validation and coherent reads within one namespace already exist.  
  Tenant-first publication followed by the shared parent preserves prior graphs;  
  there is no atomic transaction spanning namespaces.
* `src/types.ts`, `src/validation.ts`: resource tags are version metadata, limited  
  to 15 string pairs of at most 512 characters each. `envName` is currently scalar.
* `src/inventory.ts`: current-version metadata supports exact tag filtering.
* `src/grants.ts`: grants authorize environment/tenant namespaces and permissions.  
  Application name is a selector, not a resource-level authorization boundary.
* Consumer `fcrww-api/scripts/lib/api-secrets.cjs` and
  `src/secrets/api-discovery-contract.spec.ts`: finite mapping allowlist,  
  startup-loaded process values and sealed tenant revisions require restart.
* APP-48 is To Do; its original problem statement predates startup discovery.  
  Reuse its discovery/refresh scope instead of creating a competing system.
* APP-43 is To Do and requires durable `in-rotation` tenant unavailability,  
  migration with all three tenant keys, verification and retained recovery keys.
* APP-50's existing resource forms should be reused for resource editing.

Initial delivery remains LOCAL_KEYVAULT in local development. ENV_VARIABLES  
compatibility stays intact. Cloud activation remains gated by APP-47.

## Approaches and recommendation

1. Put an application list and envName directly on every secret version. This  
  looks small, but membership can disappear on a new version and a growing list  
  hits flat-tag limits. Historical version edits become configuration changes.
2. Recommended: first-class Applications and resource-level managed metadata  
  inside the existing encrypted namespace store. Keep one canonical envName per  
  logical resource and many application memberships; expose these as managed  
  tags in the UI. Derive existing runtime manifests automatically. Ordinary  
  version tags remain metadata, with no second editable membership truth.
3. Store independent application-specific mappings. This can express different  
  names for the same secret but conflicts with the user's canonical ENV-name  
  rule and adds unnecessary reconciliation; reject it.

Approach 2 is Codex's recommendation, not an approach explicitly chosen by the  
user. Physical storage/route naming is for Chris to review. No new infrastructure  
service, broker, operator file or manual counter is proposed.

## Identity, metadata and validation

An Application is identified by `(environment, applicationName)`. Resource  
identity is `(environment, tenant, kind, logicalName)`; a version is separate.  
Store the Application record in that environment's shared control namespace.  
Keep authoritative canonical mapping/membership alongside the resource in its  
own namespace. Application detail is a projection over authorized scopes, not a  
second independently editable list. Reconcile derived indexes automatically.

Managed metadata: canonical `envName`, application memberships, and per-membership  
version policy (`latest` or exact immutable pin). The UI labels these fields  
Applications, ENV variable and Version. Ordinary tags remain visible below them.  
Membership attaches to resource identity and survives a new version. Pins do not  
move; changing an ENV name previews all affected applications and validates them  
as one configuration change. Do not rewrite historical version tags to change  
current membership. Reserved managed fields cannot be edited as free-text tags.

Applications may link only names in their supported finite consumer contract.  
Initial supported runtime contracts are the four existing identities: club-api,  
app, explorer-api and explorer. The UI may create another Application record, but  
shows No compatible consumer registered and does not activate it until a reviewed  
code-shipped contract exists. Free-form schema/ENV injection or a new contract  
registration service is not part of initial delivery. This is a proposed scope  
choice for review, not a user restriction already agreed.  
Do not inject arbitrary ENV variables or browser/public values. Reject duplicate  
ENV names pointing to different resources in one application/environment/tenant  
target. Reject accidental shared-to-tenant shadowing; a contract must explicitly  
distinguish process values from tenant-scoped fields. Tenant values never enter  
shared process.env. Matching ENV names across distinct tenants are expected.

Shared secrets have one canonical ENV name across all applications. Linking adds  
membership without copying secret bytes. Unlinking removes membership without  
deleting the secret. Updating a shared Latest secret affects every linked Latest  
consumer; exact pins remain unchanged. No requirement for cross-application key  
sharing is inferred from the user's secret-sharing correction.

Proposed shared-edit rule: changing the canonical ENV name or removing a shared  
membership requires authority to validate every affected application and scope.  
Refuse the change if that authority or complete validation is unavailable; show  
no unauthorized application details. Updating an authorized resource's value  
uses existing resource write authority, and automatic publication/adoption  
validates each linked consumer without expanding the operator's read access.  
Chris must approve this distinction and the derived-publication authority.

Bootstrap retains the existing strategy selector for compatibility, built-in  
application identity where already known, scoped grants and default URL and  
development environment. An explicit existing environment selector is required  
when grants cover multiple environments; never infer an arbitrary environment.  
New tenant access still requires an authorized grant. Tags cannot issue grants.  
Dynamic grant issuance/brokering is outside this design; APP-48 must use the same  
control plane if that capability is added later.

## Concrete operator experience

Navigation adds Applications alongside existing Keys, Secrets and Advanced.  
No existing resource editor or fallback section is replaced.

Example application detail:

| ENV variable | Resource | Scope | Version | Runtime state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TENANT_CONTROL_MONGODB_URI | Existing control DB secret | development / shared | Latest | Applied |
| WORKFLOW_SHARED_WRAPPING_KEY_V1 | Existing shared encryption secret | development / shared | Latest | Applied |
| Existing wrapping/index/control names | Existing tenant key set | development / fcrww | Latest | Applied |

Actual inventory names and existing canonical mappings are displayed, never  
invented names or live values. Non-exportable `/keys` show supported handles and  
operations; tenant symmetric key sets stored as `/secrets` retain their role model.

Flow:

1. Create Application: name and explicit environment context. Explain that  
  creation itself grants no resource access.
2. Link existing resource: choose an authorized scope, resource and supported ENV  
  slot. Reuse its canonical ENV name if already set; an incompatible name is a  
  clear validation error. Choose Latest by default, Pin in Advanced.
3. Review affected applications and validation. Save records desired metadata and  
  automatically generates the required internal manifest graph. No JSON editor,  
  plan command, revision copying or secret re-entry in this flow.
4. Show Saved, Updating, Applied, Using previous configuration — warning, or  
  Rotation in progress. Saved does not mean consumers have adopted it.
5. Resource detail lists consuming applications, canonical ENV name, all ordinary  
  tags, version history and status. Link/unlink is available from either entry  
  point and edits the same metadata. Unlinking the last required resource fails  
  validation unless the application is explicitly being deconfigured.

Desktop uses a resource table with filters and a detail drawer. Mobile uses cards  
and a full-screen editor, with application/environment/tenant context persistent.  
Provide keyboard navigation, labelled controls, inline errors, focus restoration,  
and text status alongside color. Loading/empty/forbidden/not-found states must be  
distinct. Warnings identify the affected scope and safe next action. No secret  
values or runtime bearer tokens appear in adoption status payloads.

## Publication and live refresh

Use existing immutable descriptors and snapshots as the execution contract.  
Automatic internal IDs/revisions must be distinct from the authoritative tenant  
configuration revision: a secret refresh must not invent a tenant control revision.  
Extend the descriptor contract to carry both where needed. Runtime checks tenant  
control revision plus vault binding generation/digest, without manual coordination.  
Preserve existing descriptors for legacy consumers during explicit migration.

The current purpose-based resolver cannot link arbitrary resource names. Extend  
the finite descriptor with explicit validated logical resource references; retain  
legacy purpose resolution. Snapshot reads still authorize exact namespaces and  
validate kind, role, mapping, version and complete formats. No arbitrary URL fetch.

Writes use compare-and-set and idempotent operation IDs. Generate exact immutable  
version references server-side. Publish complete tenant descriptors first, then  
the parent application graph. Readers select only complete published graphs;  
failed partial publication leaves old graphs usable and new history unreferenced.  
Retry and reconciliation are automatic. Concurrent metadata/version changes must  
retry against current generations, never silently overwrite a newer graph.

Proposed transport: authenticated bounded polling of desired application state,  
using a one-second interval and conditional revisions. The healthy-operation goal  
is end-to-end consumer adoption within five seconds of save for updates that can  
validate and rebuild dependencies in that time. This is a measured target, not a  
guarantee during network failure, long initialization or data migration.

Per application/tenant, serialize refresh; discard stale/out-of-order results.  
Load a complete candidate snapshot, validate it, construct replacement clients,  
then atomically publish the candidate generation for new operations. Existing  
operations hold their original generation until drain/deadline and cleanup.  
Never mutate tenant process.env or partially replace a multi-resource key set.  
Process-only secrets need explicit adapters at their actual readers; changing  
process.env after imports is not hot refresh. Inventory adapters for club API,  
app, Explorer API and Explorer server before engineering scope is declared done.  
Unknown or restart-only readers are explicit delivery blockers, not an Applied  
status. Existing specialized OAuth renewal/CAS protocols remain authoritative.

Authenticated per-instance acknowledgements contain instance identity, applied  
generation/digest and timestamps, never values. Applications show expected active  
instances, last-seen state and per-instance pending/failed acknowledgements. No  
registered instances means No consumers connected, never Applied. Instance  
registration/expiry is automatic; an offline instance is shown as offline rather  
than counted as successfully updated. Registration cannot create authorization.  
Chris must review how acknowledgements are authenticated with existing grants  
without granting runtime callers general metadata write access.

## Failure and key lifecycle

Initial startup without a complete validated snapshot fails readiness. After  
successful startup, transient fetch, validation or client reconstruction failure  
keeps the last working generation, disposes incomplete candidates, warns and  
retries automatically with bounded backoff. Readiness reports degraded state  
separately from whether the last working generation can serve traffic.

tenant removal, or explicitly disabled/expired key material blocks new affected  
work once observed. An unreachable vault is a refresh failure, not proof of  
revocation. Do not promise immediate offline revocation. This distinction is not  
an explicit user choice and must be surfaced in the approved security policy.  
Latest selects the newest stored version; an invalid/disabled newest version  
produces a failed update warning rather than silently skipping versions.  
A disabled candidate retains the healthy prior generation. Disabling material  
already in use follows the separately reviewed revocation/admission policy.

Saving a valid new encryption-key version automatically starts its supported  
rotation workflow; no separate routine rebinding/restart step. Startup/discovery  
never generates keys. Preserve immutable historical decrypt versions and labels.  
Do not convert non-exportable keys to raw ENV values.

For APP-43's three-key tenant set, the update is one complete rotation operation,  
not an independent edit of a single active member. Proposed UI behavior: Save on  
the key-set rotation action authorizes exactly one replacement three-key set;  
the system generates it once and runs migration/activation automatically. Managed  
set members cannot bypass this operation through an individual version edit.  
Pre-existing imported replacement sets must be complete and validated before  
activation. Do not generate missing companion keys as a side effect of reading,  
linking, or saving an ordinary secret. Chris must confirm this grouping against  
the complete consumer key inventory before engineering.

Wrapping-key adoption may use version-labelled old/new decrypt capability where  
the consumer supports it. Index/control/shared encryption changes require their  
specific migration protocol; never simply switch Latest. Reuse APP-43's durable  
operation IDs, tenant locking, checkpoints, migration, verification and active  
reference switch. Prevent overlapping rotation and lifecycle writes. Do not  
generate another set merely because a refresh retries.

Once APP-43 migration starts, its in-rotation admission fence controls availability;  
failure retains recovery keys and checkpoints, but does not reopen traffic over  
mixed migrated data. The ordinary keep-working-on-refresh-failure rule applies  
before migration admission and to ordinary refresh, not an unsafe rollback after  
data migration. Show real stage/count progress and resume safely. Old-key deletion  
and retention require an explicit approved policy, including retained backups.

comments.body:
## Miami business analysis — current state and proposed business flow

Analysis requested explicitly by Lolo; no implementation or ownership transition performed.

### Evidence from current local source

* Club-App TenantSettingsPanel embeds TenantSeasonTeams. This reads the tenant categories catalog, filters isTeam, and edits season membership using saveCatalogTeamSeasons(ids, season, snapshot.hash).
* It displays current/next season and sends administrators to Tenant Explorer if no teams are configured. Its stated boundary is operational season membership in Club-App, tenant-wide mappings in Explorer.
* Legacy settings GET/PUT /bexio/categories also exists. It reads upstream Bexio groups and local team classifications; PUT can explicitly create a Bexio contact group when a submitted team has a name but no ID.
* Legacy season updates validate against configured team IDs and preserve other season memberships.
* Therefore current configured teams and all Bexio categories are different sets. Neither set independently proves that every real club team has been captured. Legacy API behavior does not prove that equivalent creation is supported by the current tenant-owned catalog flow.

Source references: APP src/components/tenant-development/tenant-settings.tsx; tenant-season-teams.tsx; API src/controller/app.renewal.controller.ts, src/app.constants.ts, src/renewal.service.ts. Read-only source inspection; no live Bexio verification.

### Business concepts

1. Club team: an actual organizational team, independent of participation in a particular season.
2. Bexio team category: upstream contact-group identity used to associate people with that team.
3. Mapping/classification: the explicit relationship identifying which Bexio categories represent which teams; names alone are not sufficient identity.
4. Season participation: a subset of confirmed, mapped teams for the selected season.
5. Completeness confirmation: administrator confirmation against an agreed authoritative inventory; successful synchronization only verifies retrieval, not organizational completeness.

### Proposed ordered flow in Club administration → Teams

A. **Which teams does the club have?** Show the full proposed inventory with source and review status. Include existing configured teams and surface Bexio candidates separately, without automatically classifying every category as a team. Administrator confirms or corrects inventory.

B. **Does each team have a Bexio category?** Reconcile expected teams with fetched Bexio categories. Distinguish linked, category missing, upstream unavailable, and not yet verified. Offer explicit reuse of an existing category or explicit creation if authorized and supported; never silently create categories while opening the page.

C. **Is each team correctly mapped?** Display team name, Bexio category name/ID, and discrepancy/action. Detect absent/deleted references and ambiguous matches. Duplicate names require explicit resolution rather than automatic name matching. Preserve existing mappings unless an administrator deliberately changes them.

D. **Which teams play in the selected season?** Move current/next season selection here, after the reconciliation summary. Show exact season and selected teams, save state and errors. Preserve existing season membership and current optimistic-concurrency protection. Selecting a season does not create categories or change team identity.

### Recommended safeguards — proposed, awaiting product confirmation

* Allow viewing all steps even with incomplete configuration; block saving an individual season selection containing an unresolved team. Do not block valid existing teams solely because an unrelated candidate remains unclassified.
* Separate readiness of each team from overall inventory completeness: “mapped” must not imply “all club teams accounted for”.
* Explicit Bexio category creation requires confirmation of the intended name and existing matches. On failure or uncertain outcome, recheck upstream before retrying to avoid duplicates.
* Mapping removals must identify affected season memberships and related records; do not silently remove teams, memberships, trainers, or history.
* Failed fetch/stale data should show “verification unavailable” rather than “missing category” or “complete”.
* Club administrator permissions and club-tenant isolation apply to every read/write; no new role escalation implied.
* Keep non-team settings in Settings. Do not move unrelated generic Bexio configuration into the team flow without a separate scope decision.

### Acceptance examples

* An existing mapped team appears with unchanged category ID and current/next season selections after navigation moves.
* A real team absent from Bexio is flagged as missing only after successful retrieval and explicit inventory entry/confirmation.
* A non-team Bexio category is not offered as a confirmed team automatically.
* Renaming a category preserves identity through its ID.
* A deleted category, duplicate name, fetch failure, and concurrent edit each produce distinct actionable states.
* Editing next season preserves current and historical memberships.

### Pending business decisions

1. Which source defines the expected complete club team inventory: administrator-maintained list, Bexio reviewed by administrator, or another club roster?
2. Should club administrators create missing Bexio categories within this flow, or resolve them in Bexio/Explorer and refresh?
3. Confirm the recommended per-team save blocking versus a stricter global completeness gate.
4. Confirm whether tenant-wide mapping editing moves into Club administration or remains in Explorer with a guided handoff. Current source places it in Explorer; the requested move must explicitly settle this responsibility.

Next stage after decisions: Freddie UX assessment in the ticket's single delivery chat when claimed, then Chris architecture/security review covering any mapping/creation responsibility changes. No engineering dispatch before applicable approval.

## Confirmed business decisions — Lolo

This clarification supersedes the source-of-truth and administration-location alternatives in the original description and Miami analysis comment 10173.
